title: Closed-form $\ell_r$ norm scaling with data for overparameterized linear regression and diagonal linear networks under $\ell_p$ bias
claim: Under explicit lp-biased interpolation, some parameter norms plateau while others keep growing with sample size, depending on which norm is measured.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, dual y-axes, legends above each plot
description: Three side-by-side line plots show generalization error and parameter norms against sample size n, from 0 to 5000. Each panel uses a different p: 1.1 (sparsity-leaning), 1.5 and 1.9 (dense-leaning). The left y-axis is generalization error, drawn as a black curve. The right y-axis is the ℓ_r norm, drawn as colored curves: blue for ℓ_1.1, red for ℓ_1.5 and green for ℓ_1.9. Dotted and dashed gray or blue lines mark theory predictions for the bulk-dominated and spike-dominated regimes. At p=1.1 the blue norm keeps rising. At p=1.5 it rises, peaks and then declines, which forms an elbow. At p=1.9 the blue norm grows while the red and green norms stay flat. The legends sit above each plot, and the panel captions sit below.
caption: Single spike w⋆= e1; explicit minimum-ℓp interpolation. Ordering across r and the presence/absence of elbows follow Corollary 4.1; the bulk panels rise like n1/2 and the spike-side panels plateau for r > 2(p−1), consistent with equation 4-equation 5.
abstract: For overparameterized linear regression with isotropic Gaussian design and minimum-$\ell_p$ interpolator $p\in(1,2]$, we give a unified, high-probability characterization for the scaling of the family of parameter norms $ \\{ \lVert \widehat{w_p} \rVert_r \\}_{r \in [1,p]} $ with sample size. We solve this basic, but unresolved question through a simple dual-ray analysis, which reveals a competition between a signal *spike* and a *bulk* of null coordinates in $X^\top Y$, yielding closed-form predictions for (i) a data-dependent transition $n_\star$ (the "elbow"), and (ii) a universal threshold $r_\star=2(p-1)$ that separates $\lVert \widehat{w_p} \rVert_r$'s which plateau from those that continue to grow with an explicit exponent. This unified solution resolves the scaling of *all* $\ell_r$ norms within the family $r\in [1,p]$ under $\ell_p$-biased interpolation, and explains in one picture which norms saturate and which increase as $n$ grows. We then study diagonal linear networks (DLNs) trained by gradient descent. By calibrating the initialization scale $Î±$ to an effective $p_{\mathrm{eff}}(Î±)$ via the DLN separable potential, we show empirically that DLNs inherit the same elbow/threshold laws, providing a predictive bridge between explicit and implicit bias. Given that many generalization proxies depend on $\lVert \widehat {w_p} \rVert_r$, our results suggest that their predictive power will depend sensitively on which $l_r$ norm is used.
